interest: This document is of particular interest to historians of interwar diplomacy and naval strategy because it illustrates American monitoring of Japanese influence in Central America following El Salvador's diplomatic recognition of Manchukuo in 1934. The rumor of Japan obtaining a submarine base in El Salvador underscores U.S. strategic sensitivities regarding potential Japanese naval footholds close to the Pacific approaches to the Panama Canal. It also provides insight into the State Department's cross-referencing methodology connecting Far Eastern diplomatic recognition questions to naval security files.
overview: File 894.34516 consists of a single-page State Department 'List of Papers' docket sheet concerning Japanese navy yards, naval stations, and coaling stations in El Salvador. The sheet indexes an entry derived from American Legation El Salvador despatch No. 37 dated July 16, noting reports of collusion between El Salvador and Japan wherein Japan would purportedly obtain a submarine base in El Salvador in return for Salvadoran diplomatic recognition of Manchukuo (transcribed in the OCR as 'Narukake'). The underlying record is cross-referenced to decimal file 894.01 (Manchukuo/110).

subfiles.about: A State Department docket sheet indexing a report on rumors of Japan obtaining a submarine base in El Salvador in exchange for recognition of Manchukuo.
subfiles.summary: This single-page 'List of Papers' docket sheet for State Department decimal file 894.34516 indexes an entry from the American Legation in El Salvador (despatch No. 37) dated July 16. It records rumors of collusion between El Salvador and Japan under which Japan would receive a submarine base in Salvadoran territory in exchange for El Salvador's recognition of Manchukuo (rendered in OCR as 'Narukake'). The sheet notes that the substantive document was filed under decimal file 894.01 (Manchukuo/110).
